newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan rubber prices hit by news of baht float.
newsitem.headline: Japan rubber prices hit by news of baht float.

text.p: Japanese rubber futures markets were battered on Wednesday by the news of Thailand's decision to float the beleaguered baht, and more falls are likely in the near term, Japanese traders said.

"Thailand's move dealt another blow to the already bearish market sentiment. Overseas rubber prices are expected to dip further as a tumble in the baht makes it easier for shippers in Thailand to reduce prices," an analyst at a commodity broker said.
Rising output in producing countries and expected slow physical demand from the main consuming countries ahead of the summer have already dampened sentiment, they said.
Rubber futures on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) dived on Wednesday on the Thai news. Benchmark December plunged by its limit of seven yen to 113.6 yen per kg.
The analyst said the TOCOM benchmark December is likely to probe a downside of about 112.10 yen in the near future.
Following the Thai government's move, traders said they expect Thai benchmark rubber offer prices to Japan to drift weaker.
"There is no way to avoid the fact Thai rubber offer prices will break under 100 U.S. cents per kg soon. Everybody is taking the bearish view at the moment," another trader said.
Thai rubber to Japan was offered at 105.00 U.S. cents per kg on an FOB basis on June 27.
But the lower rubber prices in Thailand are expected to stimulate physical buying of Thai benchmark rubber by Japanese traders in producing countries.
"Given the fact trade houses sold TOCOM rubber futures for hedging on Wednesday, it is believed the trade houses have signed contracts in Thailand for autumn deliveries," the first analyst said.
